tasks.title: School Hallway Lockers
tasks.prompt:
A school hallway has 12 lockers in a row, numbered 0 to 11. All lockers start closed. Three passes are made over the lockers:
Pass 1: toggle every locker whose index is divisible by 2.
Pass 2: toggle every locker whose index is divisible by 3.
Pass 3: toggle every locker whose index is divisible by 5.
(Toggle means: closed becomes open, open becomes closed. An index divisible by more than one of 2, 3, 5 is toggled once in each applicable pass.)

Additionally, each locker has a sticker value (Int) as follows (index 0 to 11):
`7, 3, 9, 4, 6, 8, 2, 5, 1, 10, 3, 7`

Write a program that simulates the passes and prints a report about the final state.

Output format (exactly 8 lines):
Line 1: `LOCKER REPORT`
Line 2: `STATE: ` followed by 12 characters, each `1` (open) or `0` (closed), no spaces
Line 3: `OPEN: ` followed by the number of open lockers
Line 4: `CLOSED: ` followed by the number of closed lockers
Line 5: `OPEN STICKER SUM: ` followed by the sum of sticker values on open lockers
Line 6: `CLOSED STICKER SUM: ` followed by the sum of sticker values on closed lockers
Line 7: `DIFF: ` followed by (open sticker sum) minus (closed sticker sum)
Line 8: `OPEN INDICES: ` followed by the indices of open lockers in increasing order, separated by single spaces (if none, print the single word `NONE`)

No trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:
LOCKER REPORT
STATE: 101111001100
OPEN: 7
CLOSED: 5
OPEN STICKER SUM: 45
CLOSED STICKER SUM: 20
DIFF: 25
OPEN INDICES: 0 2 3 4 5 8 9

tasks.title: Bakery Display Case Scoring
tasks.prompt:
A bakery display case is a 4x5 grid of shelves. Each cell holds a pastry with a freshness score from 1 to 9 (9 = freshest). The case is:

Row 1: 4, 9, 6, 2, 7
Row 2: 8, 3, 7, 5, 4
Row 3: 6, 8, 2, 9, 5

A pastry is a local peak if its score is strictly greater than all of its orthogonal neighbors (up, down, left, right; missing neighbors are ignored). Write a program that finds all local peaks and prints a report.

Output format (exactly 9 lines):
Line 1: `PEAK REPORT`
Line 2: `PEAK COUNT: ` followed by the number of local peaks
Line 3: `PEAK POS: ` followed by the positions of all local peaks as `r,c` pairs in row-major order (row 0 left to right, then row 1, etc.), separated by single spaces; if there are no peaks print the single word `NONE`
Line 4: `PEAK SUM: ` followed by the sum of the scores at all peak positions
Line 5: `PEAK MAX: ` followed by the highest score among the peaks (print `0` if there are no peaks)
Line 6: `NON-PEAK SUM: ` followed by the sum of scores at all non-peak positions
Line 7: `TOP ROW SUM: ` followed by the sum of scores in row 0
Line 8: `LEFT COL SUM: ` followed by the sum of scores in column 0
Line 9: `VERDICT: ` followed by `HOT` if peak sum is strictly greater than non-peak sum, otherwise `COOL`

No trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:

PEAK COUNT: 7
PEAK POS: 0,3 1,1 1,4 2,0 2,2 3,1 3,3
PEAK SUM: 56
PEAK MAX: 9
NON-PEAK SUM: 58
TOP ROW SUM: 29
LEFT COL SUM: 23
VERDICT: COOL

- For `POP`: `POPPED <title> SIZE <n>` where `<title>` is the removed book and `<n>` is the stack size after the pop. If the stack was empty, print `POPPED - SIZE 0` instead.
- For `PEEK`: `TOP <title> SIZE <n>` where `<title>` is the current top book. If the stack was empty, print `TOP - SIZE 0` instead.

tasks.prompt:
You are given a JSON document representing a coffee shop's daily receipts. It contains a list of transactions, each with fields: `receipt_id` (Text), `item` (Text), `price` (Real), `quantity` (Int), and `discount_pct` (Int, percentage off, 0 means no discount).

The receipts JSON is:
```json
{
  "shop": "Bean There",
  "receipts": [
    {"receipt_id": "R01", "item": "Latte", "price": 4.50, "quantity": 2, "discount_pct": 0},
    {"receipt_id": "R02", "item": "Muffin", "price": 3.25, "quantity": 1, "discount_pct": 10},
    {"receipt_id": "R03", "item": "Latte", "price": 4.50, "quantity": 3, "discount_pct": 0},
    {"receipt_id": "R04", "item": "Croissant", "price": 3.75, "quantity": 2, "discount_pct": 20},
    {"receipt_id": "R05", "item": "Muffin", "price": 3.25, "quantity": 4, "discount_pct": 0},
    {"receipt_id": "R06", "item": "Croissant", "price": 3.75, "quantity": 1, "discount_pct": 0}
  ]
}
```

Write a program that reads this JSON and prints a receipts report in the following exact format (6 lines):

Line 1: `Receipts: N` where N is the total number of receipts.
Line 2: `Gross Total: G` where G is the sum of `price * quantity` for all receipts (before any discount), formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.
Line 3: `Discount Saved: D` where D is the total amount saved across all discounted receipts, formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.
Line 4: `Net Total: T` where T is `Gross Total - Discount Saved`, formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.
Line 5: `Top Item: I` where I is the `item` with the highest total units sold (`quantity` summed per item). If there is a tie, pick the one that appears first in the list.
Line 6: `Units Sold: U` where U is the sum of `quantity` for all receipts.

There must be no trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Receipts: 6
Gross Total: 50.00
Discount Saved: 1.82
Net Total: 48.17
Top Item: Latte
Units Sold: 13
tasks.category: processing a small JSON document given inline (nested objects and arrays; totals, lookups with defaults, filtering, missing keys)

tasks.title: Swim Meet Relay Results
tasks.prompt:
You are given a JSON document representing a swim meet relay. It contains a list of teams, each with fields: `team` (Text), `legs` (an array of Real values, each leg's time in seconds), and `disqualified` (Bool).

The relay JSON is:
```json
{
  "meet": "City Swim Championship",
  "teams": [
    {"team": "Sharks", "legs": [25.4, 26.1, 24.8, 27.3], "disqualified": false},
    {"team": "Dolphins", "legs": [24.9, 25.8, 25.2, 26.5], "disqualified": false},
    {"team": "Turtles", "legs": [27.1, 28.4, 26.9, 29.2], "disqualified": true},
    {"team": "Eels", "legs": [26.3, 25.5, 26.7, 27.0], "disqualified": false},
    {"team": "Coral", "legs": [25.8, 26.4, 25.1, 26.9], "disqualified": false}
  ]
}
```

Write a program that reads this JSON and prints a relay results report in the following exact format (5 lines):

Line 1: `Teams: N` where N is the total number of teams.
Line 2: `Winner: W` where W is the `team` with the lowest total leg time among non-disqualified teams. (If disqualified, exclude from winner calculation.)
Line 3: `Winning Time: T` where T is the winning team's total time, formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.
Line 4: `Disqualified: D` where D is the number of teams where `disqualified` is true.
Line 5: `Fastest Single Leg: F` where F is the fastest individual leg time across ALL teams (including disqualified), formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.

There must be no trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.expected_stdout:
Teams: 5
Winner: Dolphins
Winning Time: 102.40
Disqualified: 1
Fastest Single Leg: 24.80

tasks.title: Garden Plot Watering Schedule
tasks.prompt:
You manage a community garden. The plot data is stored as a JSON document in a variable named `garden_data` with the following literal content:

```json
{
  "plots": [
    {"plot": "A1", "plant": "Tomato", "planted_on": "2024-04-01", "water_days": 2, "last_watered": "2024-06-10"},
    {"plot": "A2", "plant": "Basil", "planted_on": "2024-04-15", "water_days": 1, "last_watered": "2024-06-11"},

}
```

Write a program that prints a watering schedule. Today is the value of `today`. tasks.title: Elevator Floor Request Sequencer
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program for a small office elevator that services floors 1 through 6. The elevator starts on floor 1, doors closed, and idle. It receives a fixed sequence of 16 events:
["CALL:3", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:5", "CALL:5", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:2", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:6", "CALL:6", "CALL:6", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:4"]

The events work as follows:
- "CALL:n" adds floor n to the request queue if it is not already in the queue (duplicates are ignored). If the elevator is idle and the queue is non-empty, the elevator immediately begins moving toward the first floor in the queue, one floor per tick, until it reaches it; upon arrival the elevator becomes "waiting" (doors still closed) until an OPEN event.
- "OPEN" opens the doors if the elevator is waiting at a requested floor; this removes that floor from the queue and the elevator becomes "idle". If the elevator is not waiting, OPEN does nothing.
- "CLOSE" closes the doors if they are open; otherwise does nothing.

When the elevator finishes moving to a floor and becomes "waiting", it does NOT automatically process further CALL events until an OPEN/CLOSE cycle occurs.

Output exactly 5 lines (no trailing spaces):
FinalFloor: <integer>
Doors: <Open or Closed>
QueueLength: <integer>
TotalFloorsTraveled: <integer>
VisitedFloors: <comma-separated floors in order visited, e.g. 3,5,2>

VisitedFloors lists each floor the elevator arrived at (became waiting at) in chronological order, including repeats.

Doors: Closed
QueueLength: 1
TotalFloorsTraveled: 13
VisitedFloors: 3,5,2,6,4

- "ENTER": if in "Service", does nothing (already in). If in "Normal", ignored.
- "STOCK": if in "Service", increments stockCount by 1; otherwise ignored.
- "EXIT": if in "Service", returns to "Normal"; otherwise ignored.
- "JAM": if in "Service" or "Normal", moves to "Error"; stockCount is preserved.
- "VEND": if in "Normal", increments vendCount by 1; otherwise ignored.

The code-entry counter only increments on consecutive CODE events; any other event resets it to 0.

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):
FinalState: <Normal or Service or Error>
StockCount: <integer>
VendCount: <integer>
ServiceEntries: <integer>

ServiceEntries counts how many times the machine transitioned into "Service".

FinalState: Normal
StockCount: 2
VendCount: 2
ServiceEntries: 1

tasks.title: Photocopier Job Queue State

You are writing a program that tracks a photocopier's job queue. Jobs arrive with an id and page count. The copier processes one job at a time in FIFO order. It receives a fixed sequence of 14 events:
["JOB:J1:10", "JOB:J2:5", "START", "RUN", "RUN", "RUN", "START", "JOB:J3:8", "RUN", "RUN", "RUN", "RUN", "START", "RUN"]

Rules:
- "JOB:id:pages" enqueues a job (id, pages) at the back of the queue.
- "START" begins processing the front job if the copier is idle (state "Idle" -> "Busy"). If a job is already busy, START does nothing. If the queue is empty, START does nothing.

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):

Completed: <comma-separated completed job ids in order, or NONE>
PagesRemaining: <pages left on the currently processing job, or 0 if idle>
TotalPagesDone: <integer>

TotalPagesDone is the sum of pages actually processed across all RUN events.

Queue: J3
Completed: J1
PagesRemaining: 2
TotalPagesDone: 13
